implemented: Explicit start is required before the real geolocator permission request and position stream. No last-known location lookup or background location permission.
Pause, stop, service failure and disposal invalidate callbacks, clear location/catalog state and cancel sensor subscriptions and HTTP client.
Resume rechecks permissions before establishing a fresh session. Late permission completion cannot restart a stopped session.
The permission-dialog inactive/resume race was reproduced in the Orca iOS simulator and a failing regression test, then fixed and re-exercised successfully.

Reacquiring GPS after freshness loss originally stayed in coverage-checking until the periodic query interval. A failing regression reproduced it; acquisition invalidation now resets query eligibility. Orca iOS location clear/set verification observed stale-location removal followed by a resolved server response within the 900ms observation window.
Invalid speed/course sentinels remain null. Stationary GPS course is not treated as vehicle intent.
Only a bounded nearby bundle query leaves the device. Missing geometry or unavailable server never produces a target, countdown or pass recommendation.

The normal session consumes validated complete geometry bundles, matches directed roads using bounded course/displacement history, and owns target generations and the signal connection. Geometry is not inferred from an intersection center.

Target, source-timestamped position and road-distance uncertainty enter the prediction pipeline atomically. Duplicate positions cannot renew motion history; source age cannot become a new five-second receipt lifetime.
Catalog/session/target changes, pause, stop and permission loss dispose or invalidate the previous subscription and prediction. Resume requires fresh location and a new verified signal snapshot.
